description: pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:1559-1566 `is_aia_recoverable` matches `SignatureInvalid` as 'repairable by adding more candidate intermediates,' driving the slow path on a wrong-key intermediate. But `build_with_aia` (line 585-681) only retries on `pkix_path_builder::Error::NoPathFound` (line 606); `NoValidPath{tried, ...}` (line 609-617) returns immediately as `Error::PathBuild(NoValidPath{...})`. When the supplied chain has a wrong-but-DN-matching intermediate, `build_first_valid_path` tries the bad cert (tried >= 1, last_error=SignatureInvalid), returns `NoValidPath`, and the slow path bails. Trigger: caller passes [leaf, wrong_intermediate] with an AIA URI on the leaf that would supply the correct intermediate; the verifier returns `PathBuild(NoValidPath{...})` without ever invoking AiaFetcher.batch_fetch. Two observable defects: (1) the original `Path(SignatureInvalid)` error is degraded to a less-specific PathBuild variant, and (2) the AIA seam never gets a chance to fix the situation. Either narrow `is_aia_recoverable` to exclude `SignatureInvalid` (and let the original Path error surface), or have build_with_aia also retry on `NoValidPath` and add AIA-fetched alternatives to the pool. The latter is what the rustdoc at lines 1543-1558 promises.
title: is_aia_recoverable advertises SignatureInvalid but build_with_aia cannot recover it
